title: Build Context
description: The single as-of time and provenance snapshot a current build resolves once and every downstream script (build_analysis.py, build_dashboard.py, build_review_package.py) reads from, rather than each independently pinning its own notion of 'now' (WO-010-R4 §6).

build_context_id.description: Deterministic from dataset and as_of_time, so rebuilding at the same as-of time for the same dataset reproduces the same ID.

as_of_time.description: The operationally valid 'now' this build treats every freshness, activity and inclusion decision as being measured against. Not the wall clock and not a permanent constant -- resolved once per build, from an explicit --as-of, a carried-forward prior context, or a committed reproducible default.

source_cutoff.description: WO-010-R5 §8: the latest timestamp actually found among the current build's included evidence -- the latest qualified observation, event, collection run or manual review, whichever is most recent. Not as_of_time: as_of_time is the analytical cutoff this build was told to describe; source_cutoff is what evidence the build actually found dated at or before it. Null when the current build includes zero qualified evidence -- a null source_cutoff is the honest 'nothing to cite a cutoff from', never silently defaulted to as_of_time.

generated_at.description: WO-010-R5 §8: the true wall-clock instant this context record was written, never copied from as_of_time. A rebuild with identical inputs and the same as-of time reuses the originally persisted generated_at rather than overwriting it with a new instant, which is what keeps python scripts/build_analysis.py reproducible without pretending the record was generated at its own analytical cutoff.

latest_included_collection_run_at.description: The completed_at of the most recent collection-run manifest this build actually treated as valid (i.e. not future-dated relative to as_of_time). Null when no run qualifies.

latest_included_manual_review_at.description: The reviewed_at of the most recent manual-review event this build actually treated as valid. Null when no event qualifies.

input_hashes.description: SHA-256 of each input file this build actually read, keyed by a short logical name -- lets a reviewer confirm which exact files a committed context was built from.

generation_time_basis.description: WO-010-R6 §7. Where generated_at actually came from: 'observed_build_time' -- a freshly observed wall-clock instant, this build genuinely ran now; 'persisted_rebuild_time' -- reused from an identical prior build (same build_context_id and input_hashes), which keeps a bare rebuild byte-identical; 'legacy_migrated' -- this context was carried forward from a pre-WO-010-R6 record whose generated_at was produced under the former (incorrect) generated_at = as_of_time rule, and has been given one truthful migration timestamp rather than continuing to be treated as a verified real generation time.
